title: How a Black Hole Is Born

lines.text: What happens when a giant star dies?
A massive star shines by fusing atoms in its core.
Fusion pushes outward. Gravity pulls inward. For millions of years, they balance.
As its fuel runs low, the star swells into a red supergiant.
lines.tts: As its fuel runs low, the star swells into a red super giant.

lines.text: When the fuel is gone, gravity wins. The core collapses in a split second,
and the star explodes as a supernova, brighter than a whole galaxy.
What remains is crushed smaller and smaller, into a black hole.
Gas and dust spiral around it, glowing hot as they fall in.
Its edge is the event horizon. Past it, nothing can escape. Not even light.
The darkest thing in the universe is born from one of the brightest.
